item.title: Improvement: Microsoft: Storm-0940 runs the ARTEX agent framework at machine speed; Expel adds an Okta self-registration technique
item.description: Wiz Research independently reports an ARTEX-using actor overlapping with Storm-0940 against software vendors in October, and adds log signatures that mark the agent: source-map-then-route sequences, unsigned-JWT SSO probes and one-second-cadence spray bursts with a user agent per burst.
item.content:encoded:
Improvement24 Oct 2026 03:45 UTCrun 2026-10-24T0255Z-intelbodyevidencesourcessourcing_note

Wiz Research independently reports an ARTEX-using actor overlapping with Storm-0940 against software vendors in October, and adds log signatures that mark the agent: source-map-then-route sequences, unsigned-JWT SSO probes and one-second-cadence spray bursts with a user agent per burst.

Wiz Research reports an actor using ARTEX-associated tooling, overlapping with Storm-0940, against IT and software vendors throughout October 2026, focused on Okta, Entra and Cognito and on Microsoft 365 integrations, with most attempts failing (Wiz, 2026-10-22). It describes the log signatures of the agent: source-map and OpenAPI downloads followed minutes later by calls to internal routes that appear only in those files, fabricated OAuth callback values, unsigned JWTs tried against more than 60 SSO route variants in two minutes, account-recovery and sign-up calls, and password-spray bursts of 20 to 60 minutes against Entra and Okta with a unique user agent per burst and a median gap of one second between attempts (Wiz, 2026-10-22). Wiz says chaining, automatic adaptation to rate limits and blocks, and tests against heavily scrutinised Microsoft OAuth flows separate the agent from a human operator (Wiz, 2026-10-22).

Open finding: ARTEX: Microsoft reports Storm-0940, a China-state aligned actor, running an open-source multi-agent LLM penetration-testing framework against hundreds of organizations, with privileged cloud access in under three hours in some cases, and Expel sees the same infrastructure abuse Okta self-service registration →

item.title: Improvement: Fixed on 20 July, identified on 13 August, probed from 28 July: a CVE-keyed patch process never saw this one coming
item.description: Elastic Security Labs reproduced the chain and found that several public proofs of concept never trigger it, so a failed test does not show a host is patched; its process-lineage detection for the Swatchdog notification path is added to the detection guidance.
item.content:encoded:
Improvement24 Oct 2026 03:44 UTCrun 2026-10-24T0255Z-intelbodyevidencesourcessourcing_note

Elastic Security Labs reproduced the chain and found that several public proofs of concept never trigger it, so a failed test does not show a host is patched; its process-lineage detection for the Swatchdog notification path is added to the detection guidance.

Elastic Security Labs reproduced the exploit chain in its lab and describes it stage by stage: an SMTP client sends a recipient address with an unclosed angle bracket, Postfix logs it to /var/log/zimbra.log as an illegal-address warning, Zimbra's bundled Swatchdog daemon matches a log line of the form "Service status change: <host> <service> changed from stopped to running", and the notification routine places the service field into a Perl backtick string that /bin/sh runs, giving code execution as the zimbra user, who can read every mailbox and send as any local identity (Elastic Security Labs, 2026-10-23). Its practical finding is that several public proofs of concept write a payload that Swatchdog never matches, so a failed test looks like a patched server; Elastic's own proof of concept proves execution with an out-of-band callback that changes nothing on disk, and it says upgrading to 10.1.20 or later is the only complete fix (Elastic Security Labs, 2026-10-23).

Its detection is a process sequence on one host within 30 seconds, a shell started by the Perl Swatchdog script with snmptrap in its command line followed by any child of that shell other than snmptrap; on a healthy host the notification shell starts only snmptrap, so any other child is the discriminator (Elastic Security Labs, 2026-10-23). Where exploitation is found, Elastic lists standard indicators of remote code execution, phishing mail originating from the server, compromise of local databases, signing keys and LDAP exports, and less direct surfaces beyond the mail store (Elastic Security Labs, 2026-10-23).

Open finding: CVE-2026-73570, Zimbra Collaboration: a pre-auth command injection patched without a CVE in July is exploited, with probing before disclosure and root escalation, secret theft and cluster-wide movement observed →

item.title: Update: GitLab's critical patch fixes an unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 RCE in Org-mode rendering; no exploitation reported
item.description: Ruby released 4.0.9, 3.4.12 and 3.3.13 on 2026-10-23 with fixes for the regular-expression engine bugs behind four GitLab flaws, this one included; any Ruby application that compiles attacker-controlled patterns is exposed to them, and Ruby has requested no CVE identifiers of its own.
item.content:encoded:
Update24 Oct 2026 03:42 UTCrun 2026-10-24T0255Z-intelaffected_productsbodycvesevidencesourcessourcing_notesummaryentities

Ruby released 4.0.9, 3.4.12 and 3.3.13 on 2026-10-23 with fixes for the regular-expression engine bugs behind four GitLab flaws, this one included; any Ruby application that compiles attacker-controlled patterns is exposed to them, and Ruby has requested no CVE identifiers of its own.

The Ruby project published an advisory on 2026-10-23 and released Ruby 4.0.9, 3.4.12 and 3.3.13 with fixes for the bugs in its Onigmo regular-expression engine behind four GitLab flaws: CVE-2026-89078 (a double free when parsing a pattern fails after an alternation), CVE-2026-93577 and CVE-2026-97229 (an integer overflow in the size of a compiled pattern) and CVE-2026-110264 (an overflow of internal IDs in a pattern with many repeats) (Ruby, 2026-10-23). Ruby's table gives the first release of each series that carries each fix: the fix for CVE-2026-110264 first appears in 4.0.9, so 4.0.8 is not enough, and 3.4.12 and 3.3.13 carry all of them; GitLab fixed its own servers by patching the Ruby it ships (Ruby, 2026-10-23).

The advisory widens the exposure beyond GitLab to any Ruby application that compiles a regular expression from a string an attacker controls, says Regexp.timeout does not protect against these bugs and that limiting pattern length does not reliably protect, and says Ruby has not requested CVE identifiers of its own and that operators should track the issues under GitLab's identifiers (Ruby, 2026-10-23).

Open finding: CVE-2026-110264, GitLab CE/EE: an unauthenticated code-execution flaw in the Org-mode renderer's regular-expression handling, fixed in 19.5.1, 19.4.3 and 19.3.6 and backported to four older lines (CVSS 10.0) →

item.title: Update: Stolen UpdraftCentral keys install backdoor plugins on WordPress sites; the plugin update alone does not evict them
item.description: TeamUpdraft says the attacker entered its site with a compromised key and suspects AI-accelerated tooling, and asks users to check the sites listed in their UpdraftCentral account; Nethemba saw the stolen keys used again on 2026-10-21 after 1.26.13 shipped and reads UpdraftPlus Premium as leaving the account password stored in the site database and backups.
item.content:encoded:
Update24 Oct 2026 03:42 UTCrun 2026-10-24T0255Z-intelactionsbodyevidencesourcessourcing_notesummary

TeamUpdraft says the attacker entered its site with a compromised key and suspects AI-accelerated tooling, and asks users to check the sites listed in their UpdraftCentral account; Nethemba saw the stolen keys used again on 2026-10-21 after 1.26.13 shipped and reads UpdraftPlus Premium as leaving the account password stored in the site database and backups.

TeamUpdraft's updates of 2026-10-21 and 2026-10-22 say the attacker used a compromised key to access its site, that there is no evidence the attacker still has access, and that the speed of the exploits and the initially faulty backdoor plugins suggest AI was used to accelerate the attack, which is the vendor's inference and comes with no evidence (TeamUpdraft, 2026-10-19). It asks users to look at the sites listed under their UpdraftCentral account for any they did not knowingly connect since 2026-10-19, says it is seeing a pattern of unexpected Editor roles, and stresses that UpdraftPlus Premium users should check for unexpected plugins and new administrators even if they never used UpdraftCentral (TeamUpdraft, 2026-10-19).

Nethemba reports that the attacker kept going after the fix: on 2026-10-20 it tried the secret triggers of already removed backdoors on at least six sites of four administrators, and on the morning of 2026-10-21 it sent UpdraftCentral commands to two of Nethemba's sites after 1.26.13 had been released, blocked by Nethemba's own blocking plugin, with the keys no longer existing (Nethemba, 2026-10-19). A site that has a stolen key and neither updated nor deleted it by hand therefore stays exposed, and a removed backdoor is still probed. Nethemba also reads the code of UpdraftPlus Premium as storing the teamupdraft.com account password in the site database as entered and deleting it only after add-ons are claimed with a token, so it can stay in the database and in backups; a reader found it on all three of their premium sites and in backups going back to 2022, and Nethemba on one of its three, while the vendor says it is removed after the first connection and Nethemba has not found the samples it analysed reading it (Nethemba, 2026-10-19).

Open finding: TeamUpdraft breach: stolen UpdraftCentral connection keys are used to push backdoor plugins to connected WordPress sites, with no flaw in UpdraftPlus and no CVE; deleting the keys is the fix →

item.title: Update: PK Softech apparently kept Publica data it had promised in writing to delete; Tamedia says Akira holds about 100 GB
item.description: The Ticino cantonal fund IPCT says in a letter of 2026-10-23 that data of about 1,800 of its insured persons (about 1,700 who left in 2024 and 2025, with exit-benefit amounts and IBANs, and about 80 on disability pensions) sat on the attacked supplier server for two ongoing projects; it has no certain evidence the data were taken but finds it plausible, and it writes to all insured because it cannot exclude more.
item.content:encoded:
Update24 Oct 2026 03:41 UTCrun 2026-10-24T0255Z-intelactionsbodyevidencesourcessourcing_notesummary

The Ticino cantonal fund IPCT says in a letter of 2026-10-23 that data of about 1,800 of its insured persons (about 1,700 who left in 2024 and 2025, with exit-benefit amounts and IBANs, and about 80 on disability pensions) sat on the attacked supplier server for two ongoing projects; it has no certain evidence the data were taken but finds it plausible, and it writes to all insured because it cannot exclude more.

The Ticino cantonal pension fund IPCT has put numbers on its exposure in a letter of 2026-10-23 to its roughly 17,000 active insured and 10,000 pensioners (IPCT, 2026-10-23). PK Softech told it in the late afternoon of 2026-10-14 that the authorities had established that personal data were taken from the supplier's servers, without saying which funds the data belonged to, and the fund's checks to date found among the documents on the attacked server data of about 1,800 persons, held there for two ongoing projects of spot checks and recalculations (IPCT, 2026-10-23). About 1,700 are persons who left the fund through resignation or death in 2024 and 2025: surname, first name, postal address, date of birth, AHV number and insured number, the exit-benefit amount and the receiving fund with its bank account (IBAN), and the personal IBAN for about 50 who were paid out directly, with no e-mail address or telephone number (IPCT, 2026-10-23). About 80 are insured persons on a disability pension whose passive pension data was being updated: name, date of birth, AHV number, insured number, passive insured salary, passive retirement assets, degree and start of invalidity, with no contact data (IPCT, 2026-10-23).

The fund says it has no certain evidence that these data were taken but that it appears plausible, that savings capital and pensions of all insured are untouched, that the cantonal administration's IT centre hosting the fund's infrastructure was not breached, and that it filed a criminal complaint against unknown persons and was recognised as private plaintiff, while the Federal Prosecutor's Office and the federal police investigate (IPCT, 2026-10-23; Ticinonline, 2026-10-23). It decided to send the letter to all insured because its information is partial, the analyses are still evolving and it may never have certainty, and it asks them to watch for unexpected e-mails, calls and messages over the coming weeks and never to disclose passwords, access data or personal data unless sure of the requester (IPCT, 2026-10-23). The letter names PK Softech's other customers as Publica, large cantonal public funds such as Bern and Zurich and company funds such as Migros and Post, for hundreds of thousands of insured persons in total (IPCT, 2026-10-23).

Open finding: PK Softech, software supplier of Swiss pension funds: malware and a data outflow at Publica, with the City of Zurich fund PKZH saying its insured persons' test data was stolen, the Bernese funds BPK and BLVK and Pensionskasse Post also reporting the supplier incident, and the Federal Prosecutor's Office investigating →

item.title: Update: LiteLLM 1.107.0 on PyPI and in the official images stole cloud and AI credentials; removing the package does not stop it
item.description: The maintainers' root-cause post of 2026-10-23 replaces the earlier log-leak hypothesis: a master key committed to a public repository on 2026-05-27 and never revoked gave the attacker an organization owner's GitHub CLI token on 2026-10-10, eleven days before the release, and Socket independently found secret-stealing workflows running that day.
item.content:encoded:
Update24 Oct 2026 03:40 UTCrun 2026-10-24T0255Z-intelbodyevidencesourcessourcing_notesummarytechniques

The maintainers' root-cause post of 2026-10-23 replaces the earlier log-leak hypothesis: a master key committed to a public repository on 2026-05-27 and never revoked gave the attacker an organization owner's GitHub CLI token on 2026-10-10, eleven days before the release, and Socket independently found secret-stealing workflows running that day.

The maintainers published a root-cause post on 2026-10-23 that supersedes the earlier hypothesis that the tokens were read from the logs of an internet-exposed internal deployment: their request logs show the first token came from a different service, an experimental agent platform whose master key had been committed to a public repository on 2026-05-27 and never revoked (LiteLLM, 2026-10-23). The attacker used the key on 2026-10-10 to obtain an organization owner's GitHub CLI token, so access began eleven days before the release, and the same day throwaway branches in two repositories ran workflows that posted CI secrets to an external capture endpoint and were deleted minutes later, yielding the tokens of two further maintainers (LiteLLM, 2026-10-23).

Socket found the same activity independently from the repository's Actions performance metrics, including a second run on 2026-10-12 that took 14 further secrets, and says it has not established how the attacker first obtained access (Socket, 2026-10-23). On 2026-10-21 three credentials did different jobs: the owner's token overrode branch protection and later force-pushed the history clean, a second maintainer's token approved the production gate and a third maintainer's token deleted the run records, after the maintainers had relaxed the release rule earlier that week so that any two engineers could trigger and approve a release (LiteLLM, 2026-10-23). The maintainers say they are revoking every token tied to every internal system and vendor platform, and that the attacker's activity on other systems focused on upstream inference API tokens (LiteLLM, 2026-10-23).

Open finding: LiteLLM 1.107.0: the PyPI wheels and the official Docker images carried a credential stealer and a dormant remote-code loader that Python starts at every launch, published through the maintainers' own release workflow with stolen developer tokens →

item.title: Update: PHP2Shell: fixed PHP builds are out and attack traffic is already hitting unpatched servers; update the runtime, not the CMS
item.description: Unit 42 reports a confirmed intrusion of a European government entity with agentic post-exploitation, from its own telemetry and without naming the victim or the flaw that gave the foothold, while CrowdStrike, Sophos and Wordfence report no successful exploitation; PHP adds an informational advisory for a third code-execution path, CVE-2026-115560, that the October releases do not fix, and advises session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until its next regular release. VulnCheck's exploit now covers PHP 8.5.10 and 8.5.11 as well as 8.4.10 to 8.4.26, and Cisco, Splunk and Palo Alto Networks revised their product statuses.
item.content:encoded:
Update24 Oct 2026 03:36 UTCrun 2026-10-24T0255Z-intelactionsbodyevidencesourcessourcing_notesummarytechniques

Unit 42 reports a confirmed intrusion of a European government entity with agentic post-exploitation, from its own telemetry and without naming the victim or the flaw that gave the foothold, while CrowdStrike, Sophos and Wordfence report no successful exploitation; PHP adds an informational advisory for a third code-execution path, CVE-2026-115560, that the October releases do not fix, and advises session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until its next regular release. VulnCheck's exploit now covers PHP 8.5.10 and 8.5.11 as well as 8.4.10 to 8.4.26, and Cisco, Splunk and Palo Alto Networks revised their product statuses.

Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 updated its brief on 2026-10-23 to report a confirmed intrusion: attackers using agentic AI attack platforms for post-exploitation against a government entity in Europe reached password hashes and multi-factor authentication secrets within two hours of the initial exploitation, set up an NTLM-relay tunnel into Active Directory and attempted Domain Admin escalation (Unit 42, 2026-10-23). Unit 42 reads the markers as those of an agentic attacker: each command batch is wrapped in section-header delimiters such as ==SHELLUSER== and ==PASSWD==, the tasks are short and serially spaced, and the attacker pivots quickly after failures (Unit 42, 2026-10-23). The account rests on Unit 42's own telemetry; it names no victim and does not say which flaw gave the foothold (Unit 42, 2026-10-23).

It sits against reports of no successful exploitation. CrowdStrike has not observed any in the wild or in its honeypots and expects a reliable exploit only against a specific deployment profile, such as a fixed Docker image (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-23); Wordfence knows of no compromise among the more than 74,000 attempts its firewall intercepted (Wordfence, 2026-10-22); and Sophos corrected on 2026-10-22 its earlier report of successful exploitation to scanning and a small number of failed attempts, one of them a blocked attempt to deliver a likely Mirai-derived botnet variant (Sophos, 2026-10-22). VulnCheck's exploit now covers PHP 8.4.10 to 8.4.26 and 8.5.10 and 8.5.11 on AMD64 and ARM64 with default settings and display_errors off under mod_php, and WordPress on default Docker installs, as of 5:30 PM ET on 2026-10-23 (VulnCheck, 2026-10-21). Neither flaw is in CISA's KEV catalog as of version 2026.10.23 (CISA KEV, 2026-10-23).

PHP posted an informational advisory on 2026-10-23 for a third code-execution path, CVE-2026-115560, that the October releases do not fix: it needs an application that sets session.serialize_handler to php_binary or php_serialize, switches it to php with ini_set() before session_start(), and leaves session upload progress enabled (PHP, 2026-10-23). PHP calls it an unlikely vector, issues no emergency release, suggests session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next regular bugfix release, says a host that applied that setting from the 2026-10-21 advisory should keep it, and will publish the full advisory with the next release (PHP, 2026-10-23). PHP has not stated affected versions or a severity score, and no exploitation is reported (The Hacker News, 2026-10-23).

Vendor statuses moved. Cisco's advisory, revised on 2026-10-23, now describes a workaround for Expressway in its bug record, keeps the fixed release 15.5.21 undated, lists Ultra-Reliable Wireless Backhaul with a fix in 27.1.1 (February 2027), exploitable there only by an authenticated administrator and with a workaround described, and lists Duo Access Gateway with fixed release 3.2.0 (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-23). Splunk now lists only Smartlook as under investigation (Splunk, 2026-10-23). Palo Alto Networks' advisory now lists WF-500 and WF-500-B as unaffected, a correction its timeline dates 2026-10-23, its table no longer distinguishes Panorama, and a note says the issue applies to PAN-OS software on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and on Panorama; the PAN-OS hotfix dates of 2026-10-26 to 2026-10-30 are unchanged (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-24).

Open finding: CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, PHP (PHP2Shell): two unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaws in the runtime, fixed on 2026-10-21 in 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35, with attack traffic already observed and no upstream release for 8.1 and older (CVSS 4.0 9.2) →

item.title: Node2Shell: crafted Brotli data runs code in Node.js; update the runtime and the PyPI Brotli packages
item.description: Node.js released 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 on 2026-10-21 to fix CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in its bundled Brotli decoder that can lead to remote code execution, and Imperva ran code through it against the official Node.js 24.22.0 image via fetch() and Express 5 or body-parser 2 request bodies. The flaw is in the upstream Brotli library, so the PyPI packages Brotli (fixed in 1.2.1) and brotlicffi (fixed in 1.2.1.0) carry it too; no source reports exploitation.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLECVE-2026-111497NATOA1

CVE-2026-111497, Node.js and Google Brotli (Node2Shell): an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder lets crafted compressed data run code, reached through fetch() and Express 5 or body-parser 2 request bodies; fixed in Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 and in the PyPI packages Brotli 1.2.1 and brotlicffi 1.2.1.0 (CVSS 4.0 9.2)

Node.js shipped security releases on 2026-10-21 for CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder it bundles: an invalid block switch was reported as a need for more input instead of a format error, so the streaming decoder kept appending input to an eight-byte internal buffer (Node.js project, 2026-10-21). An attacker who can supply Brotli data that an application decompresses with the node:zlib module can corrupt process memory, which can lead to a crash, disclosure of process memory or remote code execution (Node.js project, 2026-10-21). Node.js rates it high (Node.js project, 2026-10-21), and the Google CNA record scores it CVSS 4.0 9.2 with no authentication and no user interaction (ENISA EUVD, 2026-10-23).

Imperva ran code carried in Brotli data against the official Node.js 24.22.0 Linux arm64 image, both through the built-in fetch() consuming a compressed response and through Express 5.0.0 to 5.3.0 and body-parser 2.0.0 to 2.3.0 request-body parsers (raw() and json()); execution took several attempts, and the fixed 24.22.1 rejected the same input (Imperva, 2026-10-22). A bare Node.js HTTP server does not decode an incoming Brotli body on receipt, so the request path needs those parsers (Imperva, 2026-10-22). Fixes are in Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1, whose release notes list CVE-2026-111497 as a high-severity Brotli fix (Node.js project, 2026-10-21; Node.js project, 2026-10-21; Node.js project, 2026-10-21); end-of-life lines are always affected when a security release occurs (Node.js project, 2026-10-21). No source reports exploitation.

The decoder is Google's, so the flaw reaches beyond Node.js: Google released Brotli 1.2.1 on 2026-10-21 and lists CVE-2026-111497 in its release as an out-of-bounds write that permits remote code execution (Google Brotli, 2026-10-21), and the CVE record covers Brotli 1.0.3 to 1.2.0, fixed in 1.0.10, 1.1.1 and 1.2.1 (ENISA EUVD, 2026-10-23). OpenSourceMalware found that the PyPI packages Brotli (up to 1.2.0, fixed in 1.2.1 on 2026-10-22) and brotlicffi (up to 1.2.0.2, fixed in 1.2.1.0 on 2026-10-23) compile the same decoder and that neither release's notes mention the flaw (OpenSourceMalware, 2026-10-23); it found no advisory database listing either package when it wrote, and ENISA's record now carries PyPI advisories for them (PYSEC-2026-4322 and PYSEC-2026-4323) dated 2026-10-23, which cite OpenSourceMalware's post as their reference, so the PyPI exposure rests on its source diff (ENISA EUVD, 2026-10-23).

Exposure
A service on Node.js 22.x, 24.x or 26.x below the fixed releases that decodes Brotli from an untrusted party, either request bodies inflated by Express 5 or body-parser 2 or compressed responses that fetch() consumes from a server an attacker influences, and Python code that decompresses untrusted data with the PyPI Brotli or brotlicffi packages. A package inventory can miss a Node.js runtime bundled in a container, so check the version inside each deployed image or host (Imperva, 2026-10-22).
Detection
In web server, proxy and WAF logs, requests that carry a Brotli content encoding to endpoints that parse bodies, followed by process crashes or restarts in the supervisor or container logs. Imperva says unexpected process exits during decompression and decoder errors may help prioritise investigation but are not a reliable sign of exploitation on their own (Imperva, 2026-10-22).
Defender takeaway
Replace the runtime and the two Python packages now; where an update has to wait, limit untrusted Brotli traffic on the affected paths and test the change against normal traffic, as Imperva advises (Imperva, 2026-10-22).

item.title: FortiSandbox auth bypass (9.6) and FortiSIEM pre-auth RCE (9.4) fixed; FortiSIEM PoC is public, no exploitation listed
item.description: Fortinet's PSIRT published two critical unauthenticated advisories on 2026-10-13: an authentication bypass in the FortiSandbox GUI (CVE-2026-107656, CVSS 3.1 9.6; fixed in 5.0.7 and 4.4.10) and a path traversal in the FortiSIEM phQueryMaster service that allows code execution (CVE-2026-106173, 9.4; FortiSIEM 7.5.0 only, fixed in 7.5.1, workaround: restrict tcp port 27918). Fortinet lists neither as known to be exploited, and Horizon3.ai published a write-up and a proof of concept for the FortiSIEM flaw on 2026-10-20. The FortiSandbox ranges include 5.0.6 and 4.4.9, the builds that fixed CVE-2026-25089, one of three FortiSandbox flaws reported exploited in June, so a unit patched for that one is still affected.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLECVE-2026-107656 +1updatedNATOA2

Fortinet FortiSandbox GUI authentication bypass (CVE-2026-107656, CVSS 9.6) and FortiSIEM 7.5.0 unauthenticated path traversal to code execution (CVE-2026-106173, CVSS 9.4): both critical, fixed 2026-10-13, neither reported exploited

Fortinet's PSIRT published two critical advisories for security-operations products on 2026-10-13. FG-IR-26-185 describes an authentication bypass through an alternate path or channel in the FortiSandbox GUI that a remote unauthenticated attacker can trigger with crafted HTTP requests, listed as CVE-2026-107656 with CVSS 3.1 9.6 and an impact of unauthorized code or command execution (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-185, 2026-10-13). FG-IR-26-180 describes a path traversal in the FortiSIEM phQueryMaster service ("arbitrary file write in grpc phQueryMaster") that lets an unauthenticated attacker execute unauthorized code or commands through specially crafted packets, listed as CVE-2026-106173 with CVSS 3.1 9.4 (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-180, 2026-10-13). Both pages state that neither flaw is known to be exploited, and both carry temporal vector strings with an exploit-code maturity of functional (FortiSandbox) and high (FortiSIEM) that the advisories do not explain (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-185, 2026-10-13; Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-180, 2026-10-13).

For FortiSandbox, versions 5.0.0 through 5.0.6 and 4.4.0 through 4.4.9 are affected and 5.0.7 and 4.4.10 fix it; 5.2 is not affected; FortiSandbox PaaS 5.0.0 through 5.0.6 is affected, and every PaaS 4.4 version must migrate to a fixed release (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-185, 2026-10-13). The ranges include 5.0.6 and 4.4.9 (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-185, 2026-10-13). Defused reported exploitation of three FortiSandbox flaws in June, CVE-2026-39813, CVE-2026-39808 and CVE-2026-25089 (Help Net Security, 2026-06-16), and the build that fixes CVE-2026-25089 is 5.0.6 on the 5.0 branch and 4.4.9 on 4.4 (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-141, 2026-06-09), so a unit patched for that flaw is not patched for this one. For FortiSIEM only 7.5.0 is affected and 7.5.1 fixes it; 7.6 and FortiSIEM Cloud are not affected, and Fortinet's workaround is to restrict access on tcp port 27918 (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-180, 2026-10-13).

Horizon3.ai published a deep dive and a proof of concept for the FortiSIEM flaw on 2026-10-20: the phQueryMaster gRPC service listens on tcp 27918 on every interface and does not request a client certificate, so any remote client can reach its SendQueryResult method, whose query-id metadata is joined into a file path without validation, and a NUL byte in it discards the suffix the service appends, which turns the write into an overwrite of a chosen file (Horizon3.ai, 2026-10-20). Horizon3 uses it to replace a health-check script that a cron job runs every 60 seconds, which gives code execution within a minute (Horizon3.ai, 2026-10-20; The Hacker News, 2026-10-20). Fortinet's advisory says the flaw is not known to be exploited (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-180, 2026-10-13).

Exposure
FortiSandbox appliances, virtual machines and PaaS instances on the affected ranges whose GUI an unauthenticated client can reach, and FortiSIEM 7.5.0 nodes where tcp port 27918 is reachable from outside the deployment (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-185, 2026-10-13; Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-180, 2026-10-13).
Detection
Fortinet publishes no indicator or post-compromise check for either flaw (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-185, 2026-10-13; Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-180, 2026-10-13). The behaviors to look for follow from the mechanisms: on FortiSandbox, administrator-level GUI actions that have no matching login event, and on FortiSIEM, connections to tcp port 27918 from addresses outside the deployment followed by new files or processes on the node. Horizon3 found no application logs that would reveal exploitation and advises inspecting the write and modification timestamps of a script that a cron job runs, such as the charting health-check script, and of other files of interest such as the license tool, for any that do not match the surrounding files (Horizon3.ai, 2026-10-20).
Defender takeaway
Move FortiSandbox to 5.0.7 or 4.4.10 (PaaS 4.4 migrates) and FortiSIEM 7.5.0 to 7.5.1, treating the FortiSIEM upgrade or the port restriction as out of cycle now that a proof of concept is public; a FortiSandbox at 5.0.6 or 4.4.9 still needs this upgrade (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-185, 2026-10-13; Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-180, 2026-10-13). Fortinet's only workaround is for FortiSIEM, restricting access on tcp port 27918 (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-180, 2026-10-13); it names none for FortiSandbox, where limiting GUI access to an administrator network is the usual precaution rather than a Fortinet instruction.

The fixed build, 7.5.1, and the port restriction are unchanged, and Fortinet's advisory still says the flaw is not known to be exploited (Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-180, 2026-10-13).

item.title: Update: PHP2Shell: fixed PHP builds are out and attack traffic is already hitting unpatched servers; update the runtime, not the CMS
item.description: BACS says it knows of no attack in Switzerland but that PHP applications of the federal administration were affected and that it has no complete overview of the update status; the host Cyon took more than 100,000 sites offline for hours, a UK minister reports 32 government services unavailable with no confirmed compromise, and AWS reports a first exploit attempt on 2026-10-17. Sansec and Red Hat judge exploitation harder than VulnCheck's exploit suggests, and Palo Alto now schedules PAN-OS hotfixes for 2026-10-26 to 2026-10-30.
item.content:encoded:
Update23 Oct 2026 03:45 UTCrun 2026-10-23T0256Z-intelsummarysourcesevidencesourcing_notebody

BACS says it knows of no attack in Switzerland but that PHP applications of the federal administration were affected and that it has no complete overview of the update status; the host Cyon took more than 100,000 sites offline for hours, a UK minister reports 32 government services unavailable with no confirmed compromise, and AWS reports a first exploit attempt on 2026-10-17. Sansec and Red Hat judge exploitation harder than VulnCheck's exploit suggests, and Palo Alto now schedules PAN-OS hotfixes for 2026-10-26 to 2026-10-30.

BACS told Keystone-SDA and SRF on 2026-10-22 that no attack in Switzerland attributable to the two flaws is known to it, while stressing that unrecognised or unreported incidents cannot be excluded and that it has no reliable figures on affected websites, shops and internal applications (SRF, 2026-10-22; watson.ch, 2026-10-22). It also said that PHP-based applications of the federal administration were affected, that the responsible bodies were told to update, and that it has no complete overview of the update status (watson.ch, 2026-10-22; Inside IT, 2026-10-22).

The shutdowns were large and mostly short. The Basel host Cyon took all of its more than 100,000 customer websites offline for some hours and says everything has run again since the morning of 2026-10-22; the University of Geneva's site was still unreachable that afternoon, and Basel-Stadt still had pages offline at midday and says it found no data outflow (SRF, 2026-10-22). Neuchâtel disabled all PHP-based sites, ne.ch and many commune pages among them, its IT department installed the fix, and the EPFL gave its members access to its services by VPN while its site stayed down (Inside IT, 2026-10-22). Risikomonitor's live view counts 576,549 checked Swiss web servers, 540,169 already patched and 20,231 (3.5 %) still affected, with the PHP version hidden on the other 16,149 (Inside IT, 2026-10-22).

In the United Kingdom, a minister told the House of Lords on 2026-10-22 that 32 government services were unavailable and four partly unavailable, largely from precautionary measures while updates and mitigations were applied, and that the government knows of no confirmed compromise of central government systems, an assessment she extended to the wider public sector (UKAuthority, 2026-10-22; The Register, 2026-10-22). The Register adds that government sites in Germany, France, Belgium, Finland and the Netherlands were also taken offline as a precaution and that the NCSC sent 50,000 warnings (The Register, 2026-10-22).

Attack activity began before the release. Inside IT, citing a post by Cloudflare's chief executive, reports millions of attack attempts, the first at 07:43 UTC on 2026-10-21, more than six hours before the release, and relays that AWS threat intelligence recorded an exploit attempt against a honeypot on 2026-10-17 from a commercial anonymisation network, proofs of concept and attempts by several actors from 2026-10-21, and advises an operator who cannot exclude a compromise to start the investigation at least from 2026-10-17; whether the attempts would have succeeded on real systems is open (Inside IT, 2026-10-22). The Register likewise reports that AWS says attackers were exploiting the flaws four days before disclosure (The Register, 2026-10-22).

Open finding: CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, PHP (PHP2Shell): two unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaws in the runtime, fixed on 2026-10-21 in 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35, with attack traffic already observed and no upstream release for 8.1 and older (CVSS 4.0 9.2) →

item.title: Update: Eight eMudhra CA keys were guessable; browsers are protected, Go, Java, Python, Rust and curl stacks need updates
item.description: Standalone Java runtimes keep their own trust store: Oracle's Security Alert CVE-2026-91403 (CVSS 3.1 9.1) and the OpenJDK advisory of 2026-10-21 ship the distrust update, the tracker lists the fixed builds, replacing blocked.certs or enabling revocation checking is the stop-gap, and NCSC.ch lists the exploitation status as unknown.
item.content:encoded:
Update23 Oct 2026 03:43 UTCrun 2026-10-23T0256Z-intelheadlinesummaryaffected_productscvessourcesevidenceactionsbodyentities

Standalone Java runtimes keep their own trust store: Oracle's Security Alert CVE-2026-91403 (CVSS 3.1 9.1) and the OpenJDK advisory of 2026-10-21 ship the distrust update, the tracker lists the fixed builds, replacing blocked.certs or enabling revocation checking is the stop-gap, and NCSC.ch lists the exploitation status as unknown.

On 2026-10-21 Oracle issued Security Alert CVE-2026-91403 and the OpenJDK project an advisory for the same event, which reaches Java runtimes as well; Oracle says it also applies to sandboxed Java Web Start and applet clients (Oracle, 2026-10-21). Affected are Oracle Java SE 8u511, 8u511-perf, 11.0.33, 17.0.21, 21.0.13, 25.0.5 and 27.0.1, GraalVM for JDK 17.0.21 and 21.0.13 and GraalVM Enterprise Edition 21.3.20, and OpenJDK lists 27.0.1, 25.0.5, 21.0.13, 17.0.21, 11.0.32.1 and 8u504 and earlier (Oracle, 2026-10-21; OpenJDK, 2026-10-21). The tracker lists the fixed Java builds as 27.0.1.0.2, 25.0.5.0.2, 21.0.13.0.2, 17.0.21.0.2, 11.0.33.0.2 and 8u511 (Dennis Jackson, 2026-10-20), so compare the full build string, not the release number, against the affected list; the tracker's 8u511 as fixed sits against Oracle's 8u511 as affected, and the sources do not reconcile the two. NCSC.ch's advisory of 2026-10-22 lists the exploitation status as unknown and the OpenJDK guidance as the temporary mitigation (NCSC.ch, 2026-10-22).

Open finding: eMudhra: the private keys of eight intermediate CA certificates were trivially recoverable, so anyone could forge trusted HTTPS certificates; browsers block them, clients with their own trust store or no revocation checking need an update (CVE-2026-111943 in Go) →

item.title: Update: PK Softech apparently kept Publica data it had promised in writing to delete; Tamedia says Akira holds about 100 GB
item.description: The supplier's written pledge to delete Publica's 2019 migration data was apparently not kept, Inside IT relays that the Federal Prosecutor's Office confirmed Akira exfiltrated data, though that is second-hand and neither the Confederation nor Publica has itself named the actor, and the Ticino cantonal fund IPCT says all its insured could potentially be involved but has no evidence yet that data was taken.
item.content:encoded:
Update23 Oct 2026 03:40 UTCrun 2026-10-23T0256Z-intelheadlinesummarysourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

The supplier's written pledge to delete Publica's 2019 migration data was apparently not kept, Inside IT relays that the Federal Prosecutor's Office confirmed Akira exfiltrated data, though that is second-hand and neither the Confederation nor Publica has itself named the actor, and the Ticino cantonal fund IPCT says all its insured could potentially be involved but has no evidence yet that data was taken.

Tamedia's Tages-Anzeiger reported on 2026-10-21 that PK Softech AG had confirmed in writing to Publica that it deleted the data, and that this apparently did not happen: its summary says the company reported in January that it had deleted the information on former Federal Councillors and agents, "but this was false" (translated from German; Tages-Anzeiger, 2026-10-21); the article is paywalled. Inside IT, working from the Tamedia research, dates the written confirmation to January 2026 and says PK Softech confirmed it held no personal data in plaintext and had deleted the data of the 2019 migration, that Publica confirmed the sequence (after the Xplain case it asked the supplier to delete all legacy data, including that of the 2019 migration, and received written confirmation), that Publica is clarifying why personal data presumably lay on the servers regardless, and that PK Softech did not answer and does not comment on individual customer relationships (Inside IT, 2026-10-22). 20 Minuten reports the same sequence and notes that PK Softech received the data in 2019 in a migration for Publica (20 Minuten, 2026-10-22).

Inside IT also relays, from Tamedia, that the Federal Prosecutor's Office confirmed that data was extracted by the Akira ransomware group, which still threatens to publish or sell it; 20 Minuten writes that according to findings so far Akira stole the data (Inside IT, 2026-10-22; 20 Minuten, 2026-10-22). This is a reported confirmation of the actor by an authority, but it reaches the reader second-hand through the paywalled Tamedia article: the Federal Prosecutor's Office is not quoted directly, and Publica's own page, in its entry of 2026-10-20, still says it is clarifying whether data of Publica left and whose (Publica, 2026-10-20).

The Ticino cantonal pension fund IPCT says through Corriere del Ticino, relayed by Ticinonline on 2026-10-20, that potentially all of its insured could be involved but that there is no evidence yet that their data was actually taken; it has filed a complaint with the Federal Prosecutor's Office and is preparing a letter to the insured warning of telephone and e-mail fraud (Ticinonline, 2026-10-20). TicinoNews adds, from its own information, that a folder labelled IPCT with the data of a few hundred insured persons was on the supplier's server, while IPCT, which has about 27,000 affiliated persons, says it has no certainty yet that data of its insured is involved (TicinoNews, 2026-10-21).

Open finding: PK Softech, software supplier of Swiss pension funds: malware and a data outflow at Publica, with the City of Zurich fund PKZH saying its insured persons' test data was stolen, the Bernese funds BPK and BLVK and Pensionskasse Post also reporting the supplier incident, and the Federal Prosecutor's Office investigating →

item.title: ESET: a backdoor reaches its C2 through the Yggdrasil mesh; Sandworm wiped the victim two months after UAC-0099 got in
item.description: ESET reports that UAC-0099 gained access to a Ukrainian grain logistics company on 2025-07-16 with a spearphishing attachment and a day later deployed MythicRatatoskr, a Go backdoor whose command server sits inside the Yggdrasil mesh network, reached through public peers; on 2025-09-17 the SDelete utility was deployed through Group Policy, which ESET assesses with high confidence as Sandworm after UAC-0099 handed off the access. ESET names blocking the public peer addresses as a viable mitigation.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOB2

MythicRatatoskr: ESET documents a Go backdoor that hides its command server inside the Yggdrasil mesh network, and a UAC-0099 to Sandworm access handoff that ended in a Group Policy wiper attack on a Ukrainian grain logistics firm

ESET reports that on 2025-07-16 UAC-0099 gained access to a Ukrainian grain logistics company through a spearphishing attachment: a scheduled task ran a PowerShell payload, the MATCHBOIL downloader deployed the MATCHWOK backdoor, and the next day a previously undocumented Go backdoor, MythicRatatoskr, arrived, which ESET ties to that chain with high confidence because of the timing (ESET Research, 2026-10-22). Further copies reached other machines through an OpenSSH SFTP server, and a SOCKS5 server appeared on some of them (ESET Research, 2026-10-22). About two months later, on 2025-09-17, the SDelete utility was deployed through Active Directory Group Policy, which ESET calls standard Sandworm tradecraft and assesses with high confidence as Sandworm after UAC-0099 handed off the access; ESET could not say which group operated MythicRatatoskr, and it sets the pair beside the earlier Gamaredon and Turla collaboration (ESET Research, 2026-10-22).

The backdoor is built on the user-space yggstack, so it needs no tunnel interface or privileges to join the Yggdrasil mesh, an encrypted IPv6 overlay in the 200::/7 range: it picks three peers at random from an embedded list of public peers and then speaks JSON over HTTPS on port 443 to a command server that has an address only inside the mesh, and some samples wait ten minutes before connecting (ESET Research, 2026-10-22). It runs as a Windows service with an updater-style name, and it exfiltrates files and screenshots over the mesh without staging them (ESET Research, 2026-10-22). ESET notes that hosting the command server in the mesh may prevent network security tools from detecting the outbound connections to it and that blocking the public peer addresses is a viable mitigation (ESET Research, 2026-10-22).

Exposure
Windows estates whose users can open email attachments from outside and whose egress to arbitrary internet peers is not filtered; there is no product vulnerability, and ESET has not seen the backdoor anywhere else (ESET Research, 2026-10-22).
Detection
In egress and DNS logs, connections to the public Yggdrasil peer addresses, since the mesh traffic looks like ordinary outbound connections and the peer list is the handle; in service-creation and process telemetry, a new Windows service with an updater-style name that runs a Go binary from a system or user folder, a scheduled task that runs a PowerShell payload from a temporary folder after an attachment is opened, and an OpenSSH SFTP server appearing on a workstation; and for the destructive stage, Group Policy objects that deploy SDelete or a similar wiper and mass file overwriting after a long quiet period (ESET Research, 2026-10-22).

Triage: ESET notes that legitimate users adopt Yggdrasil for resilient connectivity, research and hobby networking, so a single mesh connection needs a business-owner check, while a mesh peer connection together with a service named like an updater is the stronger combination (ESET Research, 2026-10-22).

Defender takeaway
Where the mesh has no business use, block egress to the public Yggdrasil peers and alert on Group Policy changes that deploy wiper-class tools; the observed victim is Ukrainian and ESET describes UAC-0099 as targeting Ukrainian governmental, financial and media organizations, so the lesson transfers as tradecraft, in particular that initial-access activity by one group preceded a destructive stage by another two months later (ESET Research, 2026-10-22).

item.title: Kaspersky: a UEFI bootkit ran on fully patched Windows because Microsoft's Secure Boot revocation is off by default
item.description: Kaspersky GReAT reports BlackX, a UEFI bootkit similar to BlackLotus that exploits Baton Drop (CVE-2022-21894) to enrol attacker keys and load a kernel driver that blinds security products, installed after attackers held administrator rights on networks of diplomatic agencies in Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan; Kaspersky attributes it to APT41 with medium confidence. The targeted machines were fully patched, because Microsoft's fix revokes the old boot-manager certificate only when an administrator sets a registry flag and runs a scheduled task.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLECVE-2022-21894 +1exploitedNATOB2

BlackX: Kaspersky finds a BlackLotus-style UEFI bootkit on fully patched Windows machines of Central Asian diplomatic bodies, because the Baton Drop fix does not revoke the old boot-manager certificate until an administrator triggers it

Kaspersky GReAT reports that in early 2026 it found BlackX, a UEFI bootkit similar to BlackLotus, used against diplomatic agencies in Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan after the attackers held administrator privileges: an installer takes an RC4-encrypted package and its key as command-line arguments and drops files to the system and UEFI partitions that exploit Baton Drop (CVE-2022-21894) to enrol attacker-controlled Machine Owner Keys, so arbitrary EFI files load despite Secure Boot (Kaspersky GReAT, 2026-10-22). Kaspersky ties the exploitation to Baton Drop alone; CVE-2023-24932, the flaw Microsoft's revocation guidance is titled for, appears in its post only as the one a UEFI component in ESET's FishMonger report might exploit (Kaspersky GReAT, 2026-10-22). The bootkit injects a kernel driver, signed with a certificate its issuer has since revoked, that disables process, thread and registry callbacks and ETW providers of security products; the user-mode payloads were a RAT that uses Google Drive, OneDrive or Yandex.Disk for command and control and a sideloaded loader (Kaspersky GReAT, 2026-10-22).

The targeted machines were fully patched. Microsoft's fix revokes the Windows Production PCA 2011 certificate only when an administrator sets a Secure Boot registry flag and runs the Secure-Boot-Update scheduled task (Kaspersky GReAT, 2026-10-22); Microsoft's own article says the mitigations in the updates of 2024-07-09 and later are not enabled by default and the Enforcement Phase date is still to be announced (Microsoft Support, 2026-09-30), and Kaspersky says that phase has not been implemented and the certificate's expiry on 2026-10-19 does not stop the vulnerable binaries loading unless it is on the forbidden list (Kaspersky GReAT, 2026-10-22). Kaspersky attributes the campaign to APT41 with medium confidence, resting on the identifier "xdd" shared with a kernel implant in ESET's June 2026 FishMonger report, DLL sideloading and OLLVM (Kaspersky GReAT, 2026-10-22).

Exposure
Any Windows device that boots with Secure Boot, has the updates of 2024-07-09 or later and has not had the revocation steps applied; Microsoft's check is that the forbidden-list (DBX) variable contains Microsoft Windows Production PCA 2011, which a PowerShell test returns as True once the revocation is in (Microsoft Support, 2026-09-30).
Detection
The installer needs administrator rights, so the hunt starts with the administrator-level intrusion that precedes it; the behaviors Kaspersky describes are process creation of an executable from a program-data subfolder that takes an encrypted data file and a key as arguments, file writes to the EFI system partition by processes that are not servicing, kernel driver loads signed by an unfamiliar or revoked certificate, a signed executable renamed to look like an updater that loads a sideloaded DLL, and non-browser processes talking to consumer cloud storage (Kaspersky GReAT, 2026-10-22). Because the driver disables security-product callbacks and ETW providers, quiet host telemetry after a reboot on a machine that ran the installer is not evidence that nothing ran, although Kaspersky found that the driver's tampering routines, written for Kaspersky and Avast products, failed to interfere with Kaspersky products (Kaspersky GReAT, 2026-10-22).
Defender takeaway
A patched Windows fleet is not protected against this class until the revocation is applied, so decide which devices get Microsoft's procedure and in what order; Microsoft warns that the revocation cannot be reverted while Secure Boot is in use, that BitLocker recovery keys should be backed up first, and that recovery and install media must be updated (Microsoft Support, 2026-09-30).

item.title: Huntress: stolen post-MFA M365 tokens replayed within minutes; a password reset leaves planted devices and MFA methods
item.description: Huntress reports that between 2026-07-14 and 2026-09-22 it detected 497 Microsoft 365 sign-in events in 79 organizations that replayed tokens stolen through adversary-in-the-middle relays, device-code phishing and social engineering, within minutes of capture and from one rented hosting range. The operators then registered rogue Entra devices, wiped and replaced MFA methods in 19 organizations and hid mail with inbox rules; a password reset alone removes none of it.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLENATOB2

M365 token spray and replay: Huntress tracks a 10-week campaign that replays stolen post-MFA tokens from rented hosting within minutes, registers rogue Entra devices, wipes and re-registers MFA methods and hides mail with inbox rules of one to three characters or punctuation only

Between 2026-07-14 and 2026-09-22 Huntress detected 497 Microsoft 365 sign-in events across 79 victim organizations that replayed stolen sign-in tokens instead of guessing passwords (Huntress, 2026-10-22). The tokens came from adversary-in-the-middle relays behind fake sign-in pages, from device-code phishing and from social engineering during a genuine sign-in; a relay passes the real login page and MFA prompt through and keeps the token Microsoft issues afterwards, so its holder does not face MFA again (Huntress, 2026-10-22). Replay followed within minutes, after 12 minutes on 2026-07-21 and four minutes on 2026-09-22, from one of six addresses in a single rented range used in turn, so blocking one address stops at most one phase (Huntress, 2026-10-22).

A scripted replayer with the user agent node requests tokens with the Microsoft Office and Microsoft Authentication Broker client applications against Microsoft Graph, Exchange Online, SharePoint Online and the Device Registration Service and joins 48 rogue Entra devices named DESKTOP- plus exactly eight uppercase hexadecimal characters, where the Windows default is seven alphanumeric characters; a browser-session replayer uses current Chrome or Edge through the OfficeHome client (Huntress, 2026-10-22). What outlives a password reset is the persistence: in 19 organizations the victim's MFA methods were wiped and a new authenticator registered within three hours, the rogue devices stay in the directory until deleted, and hidden inbox rules with names of one to three characters or punctuation only, created from VPN or other rented addresses, moved mail to RSS Feeds, RSS Subscriptions or Conversation History or deleted it, one keyed on payroll and bank terms (Huntress, 2026-10-22). Conditional Access blocks reported as AADSTS53003 fire only after authentication has succeeded, so they signal a valid credential, and ranking tenants by failed attempts points responders at the wrong ones (Huntress, 2026-10-22).

Exposure
Any Entra tenant where users can sign in to Microsoft 365 from unmanaged networks and Conditional Access does not require MFA or block for all users, all cloud apps and all client app types unconditionally, or where the device-code flow is open; Huntress names no victim, sector or country (Huntress, 2026-10-22).
Detection
In Entra sign-in logs, OAuth2:Token and Cmsi:Cmsi requests from hosting infrastructure that use the Microsoft Office or Authentication Broker client with a node or bare Mozilla/5.0 user agent, above all those that touch user mailboxes or the Device Registration Service; in the Entra audit log, device registrations from hosting addresses with the DESKTOP-plus-eight-hex name shape and MFA methods deleted and re-added within minutes; in Exchange audit data, inbox rules with the short names described above, especially created through the REST API (Huntress, 2026-10-22).

Triage: a node user agent with an Office client identifier can be legitimate automation, so Huntress focuses on sign-ins that touch user mailboxes or the Device Registration Service from hosting infrastructure, and it says the device-name pattern is rare but not unique to this campaign, so a device should be confirmed before it is deleted (Huntress, 2026-10-22).

Defender takeaway
Revoke sessions as well as resetting the password, because the access token lives about 90 minutes after a reset, then audit devices, MFA methods, inbox rules and newly consented enterprise applications; as controls, require MFA or block for all users, all cloud apps and all client app types unconditionally, restrict the device-code flow with authentication-flow policies, and disable user consent to new applications (Huntress, 2026-10-22).

item.title: Fortinet ships out-of-cycle critical and high fixes for FortiOS and four more products; CVEs wait until 10 November
item.description: Fortinet announced on 2026-10-21 a coordinated release of critical and high-severity fixes for FortiOS, FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer (scheduled for 2026-10-22, after recent FortiMail and FortiAuthenticator releases), found through its AI-assisted testing, and urges every customer to upgrade at once, internet-facing devices first. The CVE advisories follow only on 2026-11-10, so there are no identifiers to triage by; NCSC.ch lists the exploitation status as unknown, and the FortiMail builds are the ones that already fix CVE-2026-104286, which Fortinet reports as exploited.
item.content:encoded:
HIGHNATOA2

Fortinet coordinated security hardening release: critical and high-severity fixes in FortiOS 8.0.2, 7.6.8, 7.4.13 and 7.2.14, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiMail and FortiAuthenticator, with the advisories withheld until 2026-11-10

Fortinet announced on 2026-10-21 a coordinated set of security updates for FortiOS, FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer, scheduled for 2026-10-22 and following recent releases for FortiMail and FortiAuthenticator (Fortinet, 2026-10-21). Fortinet says the releases fix vulnerabilities found through its frontier-AI-assisted testing programme, that they include critical and high-severity fixes, and that customers should treat them as a priority change rather than routine maintenance, because AI tools can help adversaries reverse-engineer patches and build working exploits in hours or days, patch differences show where the weakness sits, and AI can chain lower-severity flaws (Fortinet, 2026-10-21). The public advisories will appear only at the next Patch Tuesday, 2026-11-10 (Fortinet, 2026-10-21). NCSC.ch's advisory describes the fixes as ones that might allow attackers to gain unauthorized control over affected security infrastructure and lists the current exploitation status as unknown (NCSC.ch, 2026-10-22).

Fortinet's tables name these affected and fixed versions: FortiOS 8.0.0 to 8.0.1 (fixed 8.0.2), 7.6.0 to 7.6.7 (7.6.8), 7.4.0 to 7.4.12 (7.4.13) and 7.2.0 to 7.2.13 (7.2.14); FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer 8.0.0 to 8.0.1 (8.0.2), 7.6.0 to 7.6.7 (7.6.8), 7.4.0 to 7.4.11 (7.4.12) and 7.2.0 to 7.2.12 (7.2.13); FortiMail 8.0.0 to 8.0.1 (8.0.2), 7.6.0 to 7.6.6 (7.6.7), 7.4.0 to 7.4.8 (7.4.9) and 7.2.0 to 7.2.9 (upgrade to the 7.4 branch or later); FortiAuthenticator 8.0.0 to 8.0.3 (8.0.4) and 6.6.0 to 6.6.10 (6.6.11) (Fortinet, 2026-10-21). FortiSASE updates automatically, FortiManager Cloud may need a manual update, and public-cloud instances follow their cloud partners' release processes (Fortinet, 2026-10-21). heise online lists the same fixed builds and the same 2026-11-10 disclosure date (heise online, 2026-10-22).

The FortiMail rows are identical to the fix table of Fortinet's advisory FG-IR-26-175, an unauthenticated path traversal in the FortiMail IBE webmail service (CVE-2026-104286) that Fortinet reports as exploited in the wild (Fortinet PSIRT, 2026-10-01). Those FortiMail builds therefore already fix a flaw under attack, and the post does not say whether they carry further fixes; for FortiOS, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator no source states exploitation.

Exposure
FortiOS, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiMail and FortiAuthenticator on a version listed above; Fortinet tells customers to inventory every FortiManager and FortiOS instance and to start with those reachable from the internet (Fortinet, 2026-10-21). Its tables name no row for FortiOS 7.0 or 6.4, and the post does not say whether those branches are affected (Fortinet, 2026-10-21).
Detection
Fortinet advises watching logs for unusual administrative access and unapproved configuration changes before and after patching, which means administrator authentication and configuration-change records on the firewalls and the management servers (Fortinet, 2026-10-21). With no CVE details published, no flaw-specific indicator or post-compromise check exists yet.
Defender takeaway
Upgrade internet-facing units first, inside the change windows of 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-23 that Fortinet suggested, after backing up configurations (FortiMail units still below the fixed builds are exposed to the exploited flaw, not only to the unknown ones); until the advisories of 2026-11-10 there is no identifier to match a scanner finding or an alert against, so the fixed-version list is the only scope statement. Where an upgrade has to wait, restrict administrative HTTPS and SSH to trusted addresses or disable them on external interfaces, keep FortiManager administration off the internet and manage devices out of band, and enforce MFA for every administrator account (Fortinet, 2026-10-21).

item.title: NetScaler management GUI is affected by PHP2Shell on all supported versions; fixes 2026-10-27, restrict access now
item.description: NetScaler Product Security says the two PHP flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 affect the NetScaler Management Portal, reached through the NSIP GUI, any SNIP that permits management access and the cluster IP GUI, on all supported software versions; NetScaler Console and SVM are not affected. Citrix plans fixes for all supported versions on 2026-10-27 and tells customers to restrict management access to trusted networks now; its post does not say whether NetScaler has been attacked.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLECVE-2026-109618 +1NATOA2

CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, NetScaler ADC and Gateway: the PHP2Shell flaws reach the management GUI on the NSIP, management-enabled SNIPs and the cluster IP of every supported version, with fixes planned for 2026-10-27

NetScaler Product Security says NetScaler is affected by the two PHP memory-safety flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 because the NetScaler Management Portal uses PHP, that Citrix is working to upgrade the PHP package, and that all supported software versions are affected (NetScaler Product Security, 2026-10-22). Citrix describes both as critical flaws in PHP that could let an unauthenticated attacker execute code in the context of the affected PHP process, each rated 9.2 under CVSS 4.0: CVE-2026-109618 is memory corruption when PHP handles an out-of-memory condition during request processing, and CVE-2026-109619 is stale request state that persists after memory is released and is reused by a later request (NetScaler Product Security, 2026-10-22). The affected surfaces are the NSIP GUI, any SNIP configured to permit management access and the cluster IP GUI in a cluster; NetScaler Console (service and on premises) and NetScaler SVM are not affected (NetScaler Product Security, 2026-10-22).

Citrix plans to release fixes for all supported versions on 2026-10-27 and, until then, tells customers to restrict GUI and API access on those addresses to trusted administrative hosts or narrowly scoped management networks, to keep management interfaces off the internet behind jump hosts or tight ACLs, and to review every address that permits GUI or API management and verify that it is not broadly reachable (NetScaler Product Security, 2026-10-22). Its WAF signature v186 covers backend applications that run PHP, while signatures that protect the NetScaler management interfaces themselves were still in development (NetScaler Product Security, 2026-10-22).

Exposure
Every NetScaler ADC and Gateway on a supported version whose NSIP, a management-enabled SNIP or the cluster IP answers on its GUI or API from a network that is not a trusted administrative one; a SNIP or VIP can also carry application traffic, so Citrix tells customers to scope ACLs to management protocols and ports (NetScaler Product Security, 2026-10-22).
Detection
Connections to the management GUI and API from addresses that are not the administrative hosts, which is also the test of whether the ACLs hold; Citrix's post publishes no detection guidance and does not say whether NetScaler has been attacked (NetScaler Product Security, 2026-10-22).
Defender takeaway
Apply the management ACLs now and keep a recovery path such as console access in case a rule blocks administration, then install the fixed builds on 2026-10-27; the PHP project's own fixed releases do not help an appliance owner until Citrix ships its package, and no fix is listed in Citrix's post as of 2026-10-22 (NetScaler Product Security, 2026-10-22).

item.title: HPE's Aruba wireless bulletin fixes 19 unauthenticated network flaws at CVSS 9.0+; HPE knows of no public exploit code
item.description: HPE Networking's bulletin HPESBNW05162 of 2026-10-22 fixes 72 CVEs in AOS-8 and AOS-10 for Mobility Conductors, Controllers, Gateways and access points, 34 of them at CVSS 3.1 9.0 or higher and 19 of those reachable over the network without authentication (eight at 10.0). HPE found the flaws through internal research, knows of no public discussion or exploit code, and strongly urges patching; its only workaround is to confine the CLI and web management interfaces to a dedicated segment behind firewall policy.
item.content:encoded:
NOTABLECVE-2026-79844 +18NATOA2

HPESBNW05162, HPE Networking (Aruba) AOS-8 and AOS-10 wireless: 72 CVEs fixed in one bulletin, 19 of them unauthenticated and network-reachable at CVSS 9.0 or above, across controllers, gateways and access points

HPE Networking's bulletin HPESBNW05162 (initial release 2026-10-22) fixes 72 CVEs in the wireless operating systems AOS-8 and AOS-10 for Mobility Conductors, Controllers, Gateways managed by HPE Networking Central, AOS-10 access points (AOS-AP) and AOS-8 Instant access points (AOS-IAP) (HPE Networking, 2026-10-22). By the CSAF's CVSS 3.1 scores, 34 of the 72 rate 9.0 or higher (eight at 10.0, ten at 9.8, eleven at 9.6, one at 9.4 and four at 9.3); the 19 rated 10.0, 9.8 or 9.4 need network access and no privileges, and the other 15 are reachable from the adjacent network (HPE Networking CSAF, 2026-10-22). The named mechanisms include authentication bypasses and command injection in the AOS-10 interface and in the PAPI protocol, a buffer overflow and a command injection in the AOS-8 PAPI protocol that arrive as crafted packets on its UDP port, an authentication bypass in the AOS-8 SSH daemon, and SQL injection in the web-based management interface (HPE Networking CSAF, 2026-10-22). HPE says the flaws were generally found by its internal security research, that it is not aware of public discussion or exploit code as of the release, and that customers are strongly urged to patch; for some of the critical rows exploitation also needs preconditions outside the attacker's control, which the bulletin does not itemise (HPE Networking, 2026-10-22)(HPE Networking CSAF, 2026-10-22).

The bulletin text names AOS-10 10.8.x up to 10.8.1.1, 10.7.x up to 10.7.2.6 and 10.4.x up to 10.4.1.13, and AOS-8 8.13.x up to 8.13.3.0 and 8.10.x up to 8.10.0.23, while the machine-readable CSAF lists wider known-affected ranges, AOS-10 10.8.0.0 to 10.8.1.1, 10.6.0.0 to 10.7.2.6 and 10.3.0.0 to 10.4.1.13, and AOS-8 8.12.0.0 to 8.13.3.0 and 8.10.0.0 to 8.10.0.23, which take in the 10.6, 10.3 and 8.12 branches the text omits, so treat the CSAF ranges as the scope; fixed builds are AOS-10.8.1.2, 10.7.2.7 and 10.4.1.14 and AOS-8.13.3.1 and 8.10.0.24 (HPE Networking, 2026-10-22)(HPE Networking CSAF, 2026-10-22). HPE's workaround is to restrict the CLI and web-based management interfaces to a dedicated layer 2 segment or VLAN, controlled by firewall policies at layer 3 and above with accounting controls (HPE Networking, 2026-10-22).

Exposure
Any HPE Networking mobility conductor, controller, gateway, access point or virtual machine that runs a listed version; HPE says every compatible hardware model is affected and that its own hardware list is illustrative only, so the check is the software version, not the model (HPE Networking, 2026-10-22). The named surfaces are the CLI and web management interfaces and the PAPI access-point management protocol on UDP port 8211 (HPE Networking, 2026-10-22)(HPE Networking CSAF, 2026-10-22).
Detection
Management-plane access and accounting logs for logins and sessions from outside the management segment, and network flow data for PAPI traffic on UDP 8211 or controller management ports from segments that carry users or guests. HPE publishes no detection guidance, so no post-compromise check is defined (HPE Networking, 2026-10-22).
Defender takeaway
Upgrade controllers, gateways and access points to the fixed build of their train, management and PAPI-exposed units first, and apply the management-segment restriction at once where the upgrade has to wait; HPE says it is not aware of public discussion or exploit code, so the order follows exposure of the management and access-point protocol paths rather than a known campaign (HPE Networking, 2026-10-22).

item.title: Arista confirms exploitation of a VeloCloud Orchestrator flaw: any tenant login, even read-only, reaches operator rights
item.description: Arista's Security Advisory 0199 of 2026-10-22 fixes CVE-2026-114625 (CVSS 3.1 9.9) in on-premises VeloCloud Orchestrator: any authenticated user, down to the lowest built-in tenant role, can gain operator privileges and reach functions meant for internal use only, and Arista says the flaw is known to be actively exploited. Fixed releases are 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10 and 6.4.2.12; hosted and dedicated Orchestrators were already patched, and Arista names no actor, victim count or start date.
item.content:encoded:
HIGHCVE-2026-114625exploitedNATOA2

CVE-2026-114625, Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator On-Prem: an SQL injection lets any authenticated user, down to the Enterprise Read Only role, act as a superuser operator, and Arista says it is actively exploited (CVSS 3.1 9.9)

Arista's Security Advisory 0199 of 2026-10-22 covers CVE-2026-114625 (CVSS 3.1 9.9, CVSS 4.0 9.4, CWE-89 SQL injection) in the on-premises VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO): on an affected system any authenticated user can gain operator privileges and masquerade as a local "superuser operator", which includes access to functionality intended for internal use only and not for remote access (Arista Networks, 2026-10-22). Arista states that it detected the issue and that it is known to be actively exploited, and the advisory names no actor, victim count or start date (Arista Networks, 2026-10-22). The prerequisite is network access to the VCO web interface and a valid session on the VCO portal; the lowest role that suffices is Enterprise Read Only, the lowest built-in tenant role, the interface is exposed by default and no configuration prevents the exposure (Arista Networks, 2026-10-22).

Affected are VCO 5.2.x before 5.2.3.18, 6.1.x before 6.1.3.10 and 6.4.x before 6.4.2.12, and end-of-support releases were not assessed; hosted and dedicated VCO were affected and are already patched, while VeloCloud Gateway and VeloCloud Edge are not affected (Arista Networks, 2026-10-22). Arista's recommended resolution is the upgrade, and for an unsupported release train it points customers to its support centre to discuss upgrade options (Arista Networks, 2026-10-22); its CSAF file records the CVSS 3.1 score and the same interim measures, and describes the flaw as "VeloCloud Orchestrator Remote Code Execution (VCO RCE)" where the advisory page names an SQL injection that grants operator privileges; Arista does not say how the two descriptions relate (Arista Networks CSAF, 2026-10-22).

Exposure
An on-premises VCO on one of the three trains above, reachable at its web interface by anyone who holds a portal login of any role, a customer-tenant account included; Arista's list is by train, so compare each Orchestrator against the three fixed releases (Arista Networks, 2026-10-22).
Detection
Web access logs of the VCO for requests with unusual URL-like path components, encoded characters, references to local or internal services and high request rates; outbound connections from the VCO host that the Orchestrator does not normally make; backdoor daemons and web shells on the host; and recent administrator activity for changes nobody made (Arista Networks, 2026-10-22). Arista asks operators to preserve the web, application, system and database logs and the file-system timestamps before remediation where feasible, and its advisory does not say that the upgrade removes a foothold that is already there (Arista Networks, 2026-10-22).

Triage: a session authenticated as a low-privilege tenant account, Enterprise Read Only above all, that reaches operator-only or internal-only functions is the signal, because legitimate operators act from their own accounts; Arista lists attacker source addresses in its advisory (Arista Networks, 2026-10-22).

Defender takeaway
Upgrade the Orchestrator to a fixed release of its train now, restrict the web interface to administrative networks in the meantime, and on any Orchestrator that was reachable and unpatched keep the logs first and then check the host for backdoor daemons and web shells.

item.title: Update: OVHcloud CLI release binaries carried a secret-stealing build for about 90 minutes; a pinned hash caught it
item.description: OVHcloud's postmortem traces the account compromise to a poisoned editor extension installed on a developer's personal MacBook on 2025-10-20, ties it to the GlassWorm actor through a Solana wallet, describes a stealer that reads AI-agent data stores and cloud and developer credentials and exfiltrates through Solana RPC calls, and names a missing release-immutability setting as the main issue; the malicious assets were online for 1h33 and downloaded about 250 times.
item.content:encoded:
Update22 Oct 2026 03:47 UTCrun 2026-10-22T0256Z-intelbodyevidencesourcessourcing_notesummarytechniques

OVHcloud's postmortem traces the account compromise to a poisoned editor extension installed on a developer's personal MacBook on 2025-10-20, ties it to the GlassWorm actor through a Solana wallet, describes a stealer that reads AI-agent data stores and cloud and developer credentials and exfiltrates through Solana RPC calls, and names a missing release-immutability setting as the main issue; the malicious assets were online for 1h33 and downloaded about 250 times.

OVHcloud published its advisory and postmortem. It says the compromised account belongs to a developer who installed the editor extension color-picker-universal 2.8.91 on a personal MacBook on 2025-10-20; the extension queries a Solana wallet that OVHcloud says belongs to the GlassWorm actor, a persistent Node.js service was registered on the laptop, and several personal repositories of the account were compromised in March 2026. The release replacement was made with stolen keys, not from that laptop, and OVHcloud says neither the developer's OVHcloud laptop nor its internal CI/CD was compromised as far as it knows (OVHcloud, 2026-10-20). OpenSourceMalware reads the same account as already compromised for seven months, which is its assessment, and says that the same actor made both steps is its inference (OpenSourceMalware, 2026-10-19).

OVHcloud describes the payload as the original CLI recompiled with embedded stealer code that copies a list of credential files and AI-agent data stores into a temporary folder named envchecker, archives them and exfiltrates through Solana RPC calls and an upload endpoint; the malicious assets were online for 1h33 and downloaded about 250 times (OVHcloud, 2026-10-20). It names the missing release-immutability setting as the main issue, says it allows developers to attach personal GitHub accounts to the organisation, and reports that it enabled immutable releases on every repository, suspended the account, reviewed write access and repository logs without finding another compromise, and published v0.16.0 with a signed tag as the clean release (OVHcloud, 2026-10-20).
